publicKeyExceptionPolicy.scope: internal-isolated-vm-test-only; no external redistribution or release

gates.detail: Current manifest JSON parses and its file SHA matches the recorded pin. It inventories the host-installed OBS tree; it does not establish portability or guest closure.
The pinned manifest contains 548 source records, 544 effective guest-transfer targets, and four explicit host/test exclusions. Its own status remains plan-only.

Seven exact cookie@0.7.2 / engine.io@6.6.9 targets remain pinned by path, bytes, and SHA. The focused PowerShell helper harness now passes 6/6, including tamper/lookalike rejection and the cross-line authorization false-positive regression; complete OBS plus Sidekick helper validation is recorded separately.

Active policy is pinned to the current OBS manifest SHA and contains 176 exact files / 258 Rule-1 hit lines. CEO handoff records the real PowerShell source harness at 12/12 PASS, 5,849,134 source bytes, with hash and reparse checks. This skips only Rule 1; Rules 2-7 and the PEM block remain active.

The exact cookie targets and the single public-key target pass only after actual source containment/reparse, bytes, and SHA checks. The read-only full normalizer now includes the pinned PEM after source-manifest identity and RSA-4096 parser checks; all other PEM paths remain blocked.

gates.detail: Separate versioned policy is hard-pinned by SHA in JS and PowerShell and bound to the exact OBS 32.1.0 source-manifest SHA. Only the exact target, 814 bytes, and pinned SHA can pass; full-file PEM type and RSA-4096 parsing are enforced. The PowerShell helper checks containment, reparse, hidden/system, bytes/hash, PEM structure, and all credential rules before the extension exception. This authorizes validation only, not payload transfer or VM use.

gates.detail: The guest bootstrap document is explicitly plan-only and lists host isolation, OS/EFI/TPM, Redist, payload, loopback, and evidence gates. The VM state/receipt and runbook steps were not rechecked or executed in this task.
The current OBS and Sidekick manifest files and hashes were checked, but a fresh full-file source-tree comparison for all 2,107 OBS and 548 Sidekick records was not run during this gate closure.

The real PowerShell helper validated the complete 2,651-entry canonical OBS plus Sidekick manifest against a unique isolated temp payload copy. Source roots and every file were containment- and reparse-checked and byte/hash verified before copy; each copy was verified again. Helper returned manifest-validation-only-passed, isoCreated=false, the output directory stayed empty, and the owned temp workspace was removed. An initial full run exposed a Rule-1 false positive spanning a newline in ws/lib/websocket.js; the scanner now limits assignment whitespace to one line, with regressions preserving same-line rejection. No actual disk-full event was induced; the first validator-failure path and successful path both exercised owned-temp cleanup.

The acceptance matrix is a source-reviewed plan only; all 104 OBS cases remain unrun, with no guest rendering, updates, error-state, lifecycle, or independent image-review evidence.
